steps.prompt_exact: I’m planning a sticker sheet for a small brand and need a tiny browser studio I can save as one file: let me set a theme and style rules, edit 8 sticker ideas, see which ones drift from the style, tweak color/constraint chips, load a sample set, and copy a clean production brief from my phone.
steps.response_exact:
Now let me build this. I'll plan first, then build the full self-contained HTML studio.

Design plan: This is a creative tool for a sticker brand — it should feel like a designer's sketchbook crossed with a print studio. Palette: dark ink background (#1A1A2E) with an off-white canvas zone (#F7F5EE), coral accent (#FF6B6B), mint (#00D9A3), and pale lavender chip (#C4B5FD). Type: Space Grotesk for labels/UI, Fraunces for the brand name. Signature element: a "drift meter" — a visual pill that grades each sticker's alignment to the style rules, turning red as it drifts. Layout: left sidebar for theme/rules, main grid of 8 sticker cards with inline editing, bottom bar for brief copy.

Created a file, read a file

Here's your Sticker Sheet Studio— everything in one file. Here's what's inside:

Left sidebar
- Brand name, vibe, audience fields
- 6 one-click style presets (Retro, Minimal, Cottage, Cyber, Kawaii, Bold) — each swaps the palette, constraints, mood words, and rules all at once
- Live-editable color palette with color pickers (click any swatch); add up to 8 colors
- Constraint chips — add/remove freely, they feed into drift scoring

8 sticker cards (main grid)
- Inline-editable title, description, mood picker, format picker
- Tag chips per card — click to remove, "+ tag" to add more
- Drift meter pill in the top-right of each card — scores on-brand alignment based on your mood words and constraints in real time; cards border-glow green (aligned) or red (drifting)
- ⚑ Flag / ✓ OK toggle to manually mark problem ideas
- "↻ Re-score" button to recalculate all drift meters after you update your rules

Bottom bar + Production Brief modal
- Brief preview always shows live in the bar
- "View & Copy" opens a clean plain-text brief: brand info, palette hex codes, all constraints, and all 8 stickers with their format/mood/tags and drift status flagged inline
- One-tap clipboard copy — phone-ready

Hit "⚡ Load Sample" to see it fully populated with a cottagecore brand (Mossy Peak Co.) including one deliberately off-brand sticker to demonstrate the drift meter.
steps.response_summary: Claude created the first Sticker Sheet Studio with theme fields, presets, swatches, constraints, eight editable sticker cards, drift meters, and a production brief modal.

steps.response_exact:
Let me read the current file fully before touching anything.

Viewed 2 files

Good — I have the full picture now. Let me map out every overflow source before writing a line:

Root causes at 390px:
- --panel-w: 260px sidebar + any .main content = 260 + ~276+ = overflows. The whole side-by-side layout must collapse to a single column on narrow viewports.
- .topbar has a fixed 180px input + logo + two buttons in a flex row — won't fit at 390px.
- .brief-bar has left: var(--panel-w) which assumes the sidebar is always present.
- .sticker-grid uses minmax(240px, 1fr) — at 390px with 12px padding each side that's exactly 366px available, so 240px fits but it's right at the edge with card padding contributing more.
- .grid-header flex row (title + legend + rescore button) is too wide to all sit on one line.
- .card-meta with two selects + flag button in a row will overflow a narrow card.
- .topbar-sheet-name has width: 180px fixed.

The fix: single-column stacked layout below 600px — sidebar goes on top as a collapsible drawer, topbar simplifies, brief-bar goes full-width, card meta wraps, grid goes single column.
